meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's essay. Why was he given a zero?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. Plenty of people draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did you ask Owen that before you entered the zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Is anything on his record right now? Whatever happens here, it stays off it and it stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote Shakespeare all the time. A bad quotation is a mistake, not a finding. What else do you have?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I've written it down. What else do you have, and what exactly are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Is that all this one shows?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. A private rewrite, to put this behind him, and not because he did anything. In writing tonight, with the zero coming off and nothing on his record.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. I'll confirm with Owen tonight, and I want that date in your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay after school on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want the zero removed from the gradebook and your written confirmation that nothing will be placed in his record. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, to put this behind him, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook and written confirmation tonight that nothing goes on his record; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You laid out the rewrite in concrete terms (private, not in front of his class, before December 1, replacing the zero, nothing on file, in writing tonight), because that met her demands about humiliation and his record point for point.
What cost ground: Nothing, though you moved to the offer while her point about students revising an outline into a different argument was still unanswered.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the essay appearing in two big edits late on the night of October 28, came close to that night in both season and hour, though it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said revising is normal, answer it directly, for example by saying what the outline and the essay would need to share if he had revised honestly, before you put the rewrite on the table.
